column17: The Women's Empowerment in Agrifood Governance (WEAGov) is a diagnostic tool developed by IFPRI to help evaluate the extent to which women are empowered across the policy cycle related to agrifood systems. WEAGov provides a way for national policymakers, civil society organizations, and researchers to identify gaps and opportunities to raise women’s voice and agency at different stages of the policy cycle, and provides a basis for monitoring progress in women’s empowerment in agrifood systems governance over time.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for multidimensional, survey-based index to measure how restrictive gender and social norms are for women engaged in different roles within particular agri-food systems in Tanzania, United Republic
column17: Working toward this objective, experts in social norms measurement from FHI360, an international development organization based in Washington, DC worked with IFPRI and IITA to co-develop a survey instrument to measure inequitable social and gender norms within cassava, fish, and chicken Agri-Food-Systems (AFS). The instrument was developed through an iterative process including extensive stakeholder consultation and cognitive testing, and was piloted in Tanzania and Nigeria with actors operating in or supporting/influencing the three AFS. The pilot data will be used to develop a counting-based, multi-dimensional index measuring inequitable social and gender norms within the three target AFS. The index will be designed to be comparable across AFS, geographical regions, and between actor groups performing different AFS roles. The index can be used to inform the design of gender-transformative approaches to address harmful social and gender norms in AFS. ;

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for creating cost-effective home-mixed livestock fattening rations using hay, grain or pod shells of mucuna pruriens and other legume hays to substitute expensive commercial supplements. in Zimbabwe and Zambia
column17: This innovation proposes the use of coarsely ground Mucuna pruriens grain as a low-cost, energy- and protein-rich alternative to conventional commercial concentrates in ruminant maintenance and fattening diets. Typical commercial supplements rely on cereal grains such as maize and legume oil cakes like soybean or cottonseed, which are often expensive and inaccessible to smallholder farmers. In contrast, Mucuna grain is affordable and uniquely provides both energy and protein in a single ingredient, reducing reliance on multiple costly inputs. When combined with home-grown tropical forage legume hay (e.g., Lablab purpureus), the Mucuna meal forms a balanced complete diet that farmers can locally produce, brand, and trade. Incorporating legume hay also reduces dependence on low-quality grass hay and cereal crop residues while enhancing their digestibility, ultimately improving feed efficiency and promoting better livestock growth and productivity.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for innovation portfolio management to intentionally manage science, innovation and scaling investments along an impact pathway.
column17: Most projects, programs or organizations do not just manage one, but multiple innovations. Innovation portfolio management refers to managing a portfolio of innovations, innovation projects or interventions aimed at delivering (positive) societal impact. The main objective is to ensure that the innovation portfolio of a project, program, country or entire organization is healthy and delivers against outcomes and impact. It can support portfolio managers in strategic decision-making, prioritization (e.g. as part of stage-gating), risk management and resource mobilization around gaps in the portfolio. It can also support strategic communication about the innovation portfolio with external audiences such as funders.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for integration of the Women's Empowerment Metric for National Statistical Systems (WEMNS) into national agricultural surveys in Liberia, Sierra Leone and Tanzania
column17: The Women’s Empowerment Metric for National Statistical Systems (WEMNS) is a streamlined tool designed to measure multiple dimensions of empowerment across individuals with diverse livelihood strategies in both rural and urban settings. While it draws on insights from the development of Women Empowerment in Agriculture Index (WEAI), it is tailored specifically for large-scale, multitopic surveys in national statistical systems.; As part of the 50x2030 Initiative, in collaboration with FAO, WEMNS is being integrated into national agricultural surveys in Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Tanzania.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for cropping calendar advisories and bundled services for smallholder maize farmers and extension agents in the guinea savannah zone _gaip ghana in Ghana
column17: This IPSR assesses a digital cropping calendar advisory system designed to support smallholder maize farmers and extension agents in Northern Ghana’s Guinea Savannah zone. The innovation delivers a bundled suite of agronomic recommendations, including optimal planting windows, thinning schedules, fertilizer application rates and timing, weed and pest management, and harvest and post-harvest guidance.; ; By integrating climate-informed advisories with practical field management support, the platform enhances resource-use efficiency, reduces drought-related production risks, and strengthens decision-making at both farmer and extension levels. Designed for challenging climatic conditions, the tool supports climate-resilient maize production while promoting improved yields, sustainability, and adaptive capacity across the maize value chain.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for controlled designation of origin for olive oil in ellès-sers, el kef, tunisia in Tunisia
column17: The introduction of a Geographical Indication (GI) for local olive oil in Ellès-Sers is an innovative labeling approach to valorizing the diversity of local cultivars and highlighting the region's unique olive oil characteristics. This initiative empowers small farmers, who primarily use traditional agronomic practices, by protecting their local expertise rooted in sustainable practices.; Focusing on agro-ecological specialization offers significant advantages for the community, safeguarding the historical significance of this olive-growing site as part of Tunisia's heritage. With its multi-centenarian plantations of ancestral cultivars, Ellès-Sers can maintain its distinct identity while developing a competitive business model.; By forming farmer organizations, producers can collaborate to enhance the value of their olive oils and promote regional knowledge, positioning olive oil as a catalyst for rural development and economic growth while preserving cultural heritage.

column16: Innovation Packaging and Scaling Readiness Assessment Progress Report of Aflasafe for Sub-Saharan Africa: Accelerating National Scaling in Mozambique to Strengthen Food Safety and Inclusive Staple Crop Value Chains
column17: The project focuses on developing and scaling Aflasafe technology to combat aflatoxin contamination in key agricultural crops across Sub-Saharan Africa. It aims to reduce aflatoxin levels in maize, groundnuts, and sorghum, ensuring food safety and compliance with international standards. By applying biocontrol strategies, the initiative addresses mycotoxin contamination to enhance food quality, protect public health, improve market access, and promote sustainable agricultural practices in affected regions.; ; As aflatoxin contamination continues to threaten public health, food safety, and trade, Innovation Packaging and Scaling Readiness (IPSR) workshops were convened in Mozambique and Malawi to accelerate nationwide scaling of Aflasafe. Using IPSR tools, participants conducted readiness assessments, feasibility scoring, and mini-strategy development to identify barriers and produce draft acceleration plans to guide coordinated scaling efforts.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for a women Veterinarian–Led Poultry and Market Inclusion Model, Embedded within a Media-Driven Social Norms and Demand Creation Strategy (Maisha Makutano)
column17: This innovation package integrates women veterinarian–led poultry and animal health services with a structured market inclusion model and a media-driven social norms change strategy. It combines gender-accommodative approaches—strengthening women veterinarians’ business, technical, and service delivery capacities—with gender-transformative strategies designed to shift restrictive norms that limit women’s participation in poultry enterprises.; ; Beyond service delivery, the model embeds an edutainment and media platform to build trust, reshape perceptions of women as credible animal health professionals, normalize women’s leadership in poultry markets, and stimulate demand among farming households. By pairing capacity strengthening with deliberate narrative and visibility strategies, the package addresses both the practical constraints women face and the underlying social norms that sustain gender-based disadvantage, aiming for durable behavioral and market-system change rather than short-term inclusion.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for restoring rangelands: the art of flexible livestock grazing to restore soil health, ecosystem function and ecosystem services  in Tunisia
column17: Nomadic livestock systems have evolved over millennia as a response to seasonal rainfall patterns. In Tunisia, where approximately one-third of the land is semi-arid, arid, or desert, degradation poses a significant challenge. The Gdel resting technique, a low-cost intervention, has been part of the national strategy for rangeland improvement Since 1990, this practice is implemented by developing agencies for rangeland improvement. The pastoralists whose animals would normally graze in these areas are supported through the provision of feed supplements for 3 consecutive years. However, the implementation had its shortfalls. However, in 2018, unexpectedly high rainfall led to abundant vegetation growth, but the rigid implementation of the resting technique hindered pastoralists from capitalizing on the surplus biomass. In response, ICARDA developed flexible grazing criteria and trained partners to adapt to climate variability. This innovative approach allows pastoralists to optimize resource utilization during favorable years and addressing the shortcomings of previous implementations.

column17: OFSP puree is a smooth, mashed form of the Orange-Fleshed Sweet Potato. OFSP puree serves as a base ingredient in various recipes. It is used in making baby food, soups, stews, and sauces. In Malawi, the innovation is being promoted as a key ingredient in the commercial sector for nutritious products as bread, buns, fritters, and doughnuts in replacement of up to 30% wheat flour. Less sugar is used. In the food and nutrition area, the innovation is promoted in school feeding program, where puree is one third in replacing corn-soy flour porridges. In addition to taste, learners preference high due to the golden appearance. OFSP puree acts as a nutritious component that enhances the nutritional content of dishes while providing the health benefits associated with the high beta-carotene content found in Orange-Fleshed Sweet Potatoes.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for measuring, reporting and verification (mrv) framework for monitoring deforestation emissions from colombia in Colombia
column17: The MRV Protocol has been adopted and implemented by government institutions and private sector actors as a standardized system to monitor, report, and verify zero-deforestation commitments in Colombia’s cocoa and livestock supply chains. The Ministry of Agriculture formally submitted the MRV as a new Means of Implementation under Colombia’s NDC 3.0, while an Interministerial Resolution is under development to institutionalize its application nationwide.; At the operational level, companies and producer organizations are applying the MRV across more than 1,200 farms, using geospatial analysis aligned with IDEAM’s official deforestation datasets. This adoption strengthens traceability, supports compliance with emerging regulations such as EUDR, and enables measurable reporting of deforestation risk and avoided emissions. The innovation has transitioned from pilot implementation to structured national scaling, demonstrating sustained and validated use under real-world conditions.

column17: Participatory Rangeland Management (PRM) is a defined step-by-step process for improving local level rangeland management by local pastoralist communities. It follows three stages of investigation (including participatory mapping), negotiation and implementation. It supports establishment and/or strengthening of rangelands management institutions, and supports the production of a rangeland management plan and an agreement with local government to improve access of communities to natural resources and land. M&E and capacity building are also important steps.

column17: Smallholder mechanization helps to reduce production cost and drudgery making agriculture more attractive to the youth. Successful mechanization in most of the African countries relies on selection, validation, piloting, and scaling of appropriate inexpensive machinery solutions adapted to farm size and financial ability of smallholder farmers. Over the past decade, CIMMYT has tested, validated, and piloted small scale machinery and business models suitable for southern African farmers. Currently there more than 300 mechanization service providers are operating their businesses in Zimbabwe, Zambia and Malawi.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for Feed pellet production for ruminants using a small-scale pelletizer and locally available agricultural products and agroindustrial by-products to replace expensive imported concentrates and reduce production costs, For agro-pastoralists (improved feed) and farmer organizations (income generation) in Northern Africa
column17: Compressing local agro-industrial by products into nutrient dense livestock feed pellets is a worthwhile innovation to compete with expensive and imported feed pellets or concentrates. Use of such pellets also alleviates pressure on rangelands or grasslands.  This innovation consists of a small scale compressor 'pelletizer' and formulas to create qualitatively suﬃcient feed pellets with locally available inputs. In Tunisia, there are many agro-pastoralists that are dependent on expensive and imported livestock feed pellets to improve livestock quality and to supplement feed shortages. Risks of relative feed shortages are likely to increase due to climate change. Also there are many discarded by-products from local agro-food supply chains such as olive cakes, date kernels, and downgraded dates, which still contain nutrients. Feed pellet production with this small scale pelletizer producing 500 kg pellets / hour is also an interesting income generating activity for farmer organizations and creates employment.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for decision support tool for right sizing of solar-powered irrigation pumps in Africa and South Asia in Nepal
column17: In 2022, IWMI partnered with the Indian Council of Agricultural Research (ICAR) and the Borlaug Institute for South Asia (BISA) to jointly develop the solar irrigation pump (SIP) sizing tool for India. The tool, developed with support from GIZ, was designed specifically for the Government of India, for use in the ambitious agri-solarization initiative PM-KUSUM ("Pradhan Mantri Kisan Urja Suraksha evam Utthaan Mahabhiyan'). The Excel-based beta version of the tool and the user manual are available online. The tool has since been adopted by PM-KUSUM and web and mobile versions of the tool are being developed. IWMI and ICAR have committed to promote large-scale use and deployment of the tool and support future versions. As part of NEXUS Gains, the SIP sizing tool has been identified as one of the innovations to be scaled, including by extending its use beyond India. In 2023-2024, IWMI in partnership with GIZ Nepal and the Alternative Energy Promotion Center (AEPC) have developed a "Solar Pump Sizing Tool" for Nepal and launched in a Global Science-Policy Forum held in Kathmandu on 25th April 2024. column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for a set of software tools will enable quick coarse-scale desktop estimates of the environmental flow requirements of rivers in Nepal
column17: The Environmental Flow Estimation Tools are a set of user-friendly (online and offline) software tools enabling desktop estimation of quick, coarse-scale environmental flow requirements of rivers. The input data required are time series data of monthly “natural” river flows, either measured or estimated. The tools are meant to be used by water planners and managers in making initial planning-level estimates of environmental flows, which may then be followed by more comprehensive assessments using further data related to aquatic ecology, moving beyond river flow data. Five tools are currently available, two covering major rivers and the other three specifically for estimating environmental flow requirements in Nepal. The tools are also useful for building capacity on environmental flow estimation, including for students and practitioners seeking to gain an initial understanding of the concept; of environmental flows.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for tools for pioneer farmer-led scaling and knowledge network development by pioneer farmers, researchers, extension, private and development actors for outscaling on-farm adaptation to climate change. in Ethiopia
column17: We work with pioneers of adaptation to climate change in livestock production. Pioneers of adaptation are farmers who have developed their adaptation practices with their own endogenous innovations beyond piloting stage. We support them in developing a farm-level adapted scaling approach complementary to existing institutions, involving pioneers themselves as the main actors in the scaling process. Together with the pioneers we study their practices, and then progressively include more farmers, farmer groups, cooperatives in a knowledge exchange through participatory field days where pioneers share and discuss the findings of this data collection on their practices. Gradually, we develop a Farmer2Farmer knowledge network that connects pioneers and their learning groups with research, extension, development organisations, and private sector actors.

column17: The 'GANSO Endorsement' is a voluntary evaluation tool for livestock producers. It was developed by the GANSO (GANadería SOstenible / Sustainable Livestock) organization, co-founded by the Alliance Bioversity-CIAT. This organization was created to improve the livestock production systems in the Colombian Eastern Plains, from extensive degraded pastures and soils to productive and sustainable landscapes.  The endorsement has grown and developed as a set of 5 pillars (environment, people, animal welfare, management & meat quality) and 52 practices that are independently assessed and categorized in order of their compliance level. This gives the farmers incentives to sell beef at a premium price, supported by the consumers' willingness to pay for environmental-friendly products. These products are currently available in one of Colombia's largest retailers, in 182 stores located in 6 cities.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for financial tool targeted to help pastoralists cope with drought related risks in the drylands of Africa  in Ethiopia
column17: Index-based drought risk financing and insurance (IBDRFI) instruments trigger payouts/financial response based on an ‘objective’ index approximating the impact/loss. The products have been designed to protect pastoralists in the face of drought. In Index-based livestock insurance (IBLI) products, Normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) time series are elaborated to obtain an area-aggregated index of relative seasonal forage availability. When the index falls below a pre-defined threshold, payouts are triggered and increase proportionally to the severity of estimated forage scarcity. This assumes that, when forage is scarce, grazing resources are depleted quickly, leading to deteriorating livestock conditions and increased livestock mortality. Pastoralists could use the payouts to make production decisions that reduce their herd losses during the drought including, purchasing animal fodder, water or veterinary services. IBDRFI initiatives have been implemented in Africa with different modalities, including retail microinsurance products, macrolevel insurance schemes for social livelihood protection, or social safety net programs.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for participatory land use planning across administrative borders in pastoral areas for protecting shared grazing lands and other resources. in Tanzania, United Republic
column17: Participatory land use planning (PLUP) for pastoral areas overcomes many of the challenges of conventional land use planning including creating hard boundaries around villages or other administrative units, breaking up and limiting; or preventing access to shared grazing lands and water points. PLUP for pastoral areas aims to keep rangelands; and particularly grazing lands intact working across administrative boundaries through joint PLUP agreements strengthening reciprocal relations, collective tenure and good governance and resolving and preventing conflicts between land users. Pastoral communities, traditionally marginalized from the village PLUP process, stand to benefit significantly from this approach due to its greater inclusivity of all land users in the planning and decision-making processes. The PLUP process includes the collection of data for assessing land potential most relevant for pastoral systems.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for atmospheric water harvesting for refugee host communities in Jordan
column17: Mega-WaHa is a state-of-the-art device that will, on average, produce 500 liters of pure water every day directly from the air regardless of the region, climate, or environmental conditions. This device is deployed to support water security in refugee-host communities in Jordan. The Mega-WaHa will supply at least 182,500 liters (182 m3) of fresh water in 2025 for crop production. The innovation will save Jordan an equivalent amount of water from the country's water supply thereby demonstrating that this new technology, if adopted widely, has the potential to significantly increase water security for the country.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for vertical farming for host communities in Jordan
column17: GreenSpin is a vertical farming unit technology that integrates natural sunlight and renewable energy sources into an indoor and controlled environment agriculture (CEA), promoting sustainable and energy-efficient farming practices. By leveraging these technologies, the project aims to achieve a 70% reduction in water usage compared to traditional agriculture and a 60% reduction in energy consumption compared to current vertical farming methods. The GreenSpin farming unit will further contribute to a 50-70% increase in crop production efficiency in limited spaces, advancing sustainable urban agriculture within challenged communities.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for climate-related risk maps and adaptation plans (CS-MAP) for rice production in Bangladesh
column17: Climate smart maps (CS-MAP) has been developed based on participatory mapping approach that integrates local knowledge and science-based researches, for ten districts in the coastal region of Bangladesh, these are: Khulna, Satkhira, Patuakhali, Barguna, Bagerhat, Pirojpur, Narail, Gopalganj, Barishal and Bhola. These CS-MAP provide climate-related risks and location-specific adaptation plans for crop production and act as decision support tools. They are expected to make a remarkable contribution to the goal of the CGIAR initiative on Asian Mega-Deltas (AMD).. The scaling readiness assessment has been carried out for climate smart risk map tool and its implementation enablers through a 1-day workshop. As the first step of the preparation phase, the partners and stakeholders were identified for scaling the readiness of CS-MAPs and their enablers, followed by ensuring the participation of key internal decision-makers, obtaining necessary approvals and notifications, determining the context of the package, and developing a scaling ambition.

column17: Participatory Rangeland Management (PRM) is a defined step-by-step process for improving local level rangeland management by local pastoralist communities. It follows three stages of investigation (including participatory mapping), negotiation and implementation. It supports establishment and/or strengthening of rangelands management institutions, and supports the production of a rangeland management plan and an agreement with local government to improve access of communities to natural resources and land. M&E and capacity building are also important steps.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for innovative software tools for estimating environmental flow requirements based on monthly river flow time series in Pakistan
column17: The Environmental Flow Assessment Tools are a set of user-friendly (online and offline) software tools enabling quick estimation of coarsescale environmental flow requirements of rivers. The input data required are time series data of monthly “natural” river flows, either measured or estimated. The tools are meant to be used by water planners and managers in making initial planning-level estimates of environmental flows, which may then be followed by more comprehensive assessments using further data related to aquatic ecology, moving beyond river flow data. IWMI has already developed five such tools, two covering major rivers and the other three specifically for estimating environmental flow requirements in the Ganges River Basin in Sri Lanka and Nepal, and is now expanding to the Indus River Basin in Pakistan. The tools are also useful for building capacity on environmental flow estimation, including for students and practitioners seeking to gain an initial understanding of the concept of environmental flows. The IPSR assessment conducted in Pakistan is a first step towards understanding the enabling environment for scaling this innovation and identifying complementary innovations required for scaling.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for strip cropping is an improved intercropping strategy for smallholder farmers that capitalize on a better plant arrangement. two types of strip cropping are common: double-row strip cropping and four row strip cropping. in Zambia, Zimbabwe and Malawi
column17: Double-row strip cropping: This system reduces the plant spacing of maize rows to open up space for legumes to grow. Maize is usually intercropped with a legume (i.e., groundnuts/soya beans/cowpeas/beans). Maize is planted into rip-lines opened in double rows (50cm inter-row x 25cm in-row) and a gap of 130cm is left in-between the maize double rows where legumes will be planted [groundnut (35cm inter-row x 30cm in-row); soya beans (35cm inter-row x 5cm in-row)]Four-row strip cropping: Similar to double row strip cropping above, four rows of maize alternate with four rows of a legume. However, the inter-row spacing of maize is reduced from the usual 90 cm to 45 cm. This narrowing and reduction in size increases growing space for four rows of legumes. Maize is planted into lines spaced at 45 cm inter-row with 4 row strips of maize alternating with another 4 rows strip of soya beans/groundnuts also spaced at 45 cm between rows.

column17: Conservation Agriculture (CA) is based on three key principles: minimum soil disturbance, provision of permanent soil cover and the use of rotations or associations amongst other good agriculture practices. These CA principles are applicable to a wide range of crop production systems from low-yielding, rainfed conditions to high-yielding, irrigated conditions. However, the techniques used may vary from place to place depending on farm power, system management conditions and farmer circumstances. CA aims at rebuilding the soil, optimizing crop production inputs especially labour, and increasing profits. The social and economic benefits gained from combining production and protecting the environment under CA, including reduced input and labour costs, are greater than those from production alone. With CA, farming communities become providers of more healthy living environments for the wider community through reduced use of fossil fuels and through conservation of environmental integrity and services.

column17: The Groundwater Management Information System (GMIS) is a web-based data-driven decision-support platform that will help policy makers and implementers to better manage, analyze, and report on groundwater data. The innovation is currently piloted in Punjab, Pakistan to support the Punjab Water Services Regulatory Authority, established under the Punjab Water Act 2019. It will be further upscaled to the country level in order to support implementation of National and provincial water policies. The IPSR assessment was conducted with diverse stakeholder from Pubjab and other provinces in Pakistan to help to understand the enabling environment and scaling for this innovation.

column17: Participatory Rangeland Management (PRM) is a defined step-by-step process for improving local level rangeland management by local pastoralist communities. It follows three stages of investigation (including participatory mapping), negotiation and implementation. It supports establishment and/or strengthening of rangelands management institutions, and supports the production of a rangeland management plan and an agreement with local government to improve access of communities to natural resources and land. M&E and capacity building are also important steps.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for Climate-credit risk scoring system for livestock production systems to guide adaptation finance in Eastern Africa
column17: ShambaShield explores design and market opportunities to bundle financial protection, literacy, and inclusivity services to enhance climate resilience for farmers in Kenya. Bundling opportunities are assessed for existing innovations a) Climate-Credit Scoring Tool:  tool to assesses farmer's creditworthiness by incorporating climate risk factors, farm management practices, and unlock financing, b) Digital Agro-Advisory Services and Edutainment Shows: farmers receive tailored advice on best agricultural practices and financial literacy through shows and mobile devices, c) combining credit with weather risk insurance, creating an integrated safety net within the loans that mitigates risks for both farmers and lenders. Together, these elements form a robust framework aimed at enhancing the sustainability and productivity of farming under changing climatic conditions.;

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for dynamic evolutionary populations of productivity of mixtures of different of barley in ethiopian highlands in Nepal, Bhutan, Iran (Islamic Republic of), Jordan, Uganda and Ethiopia
column17: Maintaining inter-varietal crop diversity, created through evolutionary plant breeding (EPB), on farms is proven to improve farmers productivity, resilience to climate change and enhance dietary diversity. We have tested evolutionary populations created through Evolutionary Plant Breeding in Ethiopia, Bhutan, Iran, Jordan, Nepal and Uganda for four crops: Barley, beans, wheat and rice and identified superior performing populations under different farming systems. Integration of evolutionary plant breeding to Sustainable Intensification of Mixed farming System (SI-MFS) in target countries is important to sustain crop production sector of target farming systems. At least one composite or mixture population is developed for each country targeted by the SI-MFS initiative.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for high-quality peste des petits ruminants (ppr) thermotolerant vaccine to reduce small ruminant mortality in Mali
column17: Since 2016, the International Livestock Research Institute has partnered with Hester Biosciences Ltd of India, a private vaccine production company, to support the Central Veterinary Laboratory of Mali in optimizing and producing thermotolerant vaccine called “ILRI thermotolerant Peste des Petits Ruminants vaccine produced by the Thermovac process” developed by Internationa Livestock Research Institute and referred here as “ILRI protocol”. The proposed vaccine has proved considerably stable at ambient temperatures up to seven days, which has tremendous advantage in hot countries and in remote areas. The project has gone beyond technology development to identify and test components of new institutional model for delivering effective Peste des Petits Ruminants control services to small ruminant producers in Mali

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for community-designed one health units as a model for integrated human, animal and environment health service delivery to pastoralists in the horn of africa in Ethiopia
column17: The One Health Unit (OHU) serves as a collaboration and coordination platform for frontline service providers and community-based actors to deliver integrated services to improve the health of humans, animals and the environment. In mobile OHUs, frontline service providers move along pastoralist/livestock routes, according to a monthly schedule, changing sites every day and responding to the needs of the population in a certain site/location. In static OHUs, frontline service providers work side by side in a common facility (e.g., human/animal health post, water point or other village gathering site). The OHU is generally staffed by government employees from different sectors who are released from their regular duties to deliver integrated services through the OHU. The services are targeted towards pastoralist and agropastoralist communities, their livestock, and the rangelands which they access, with a particular focus on vulnerable and hard-to-reach communities.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for Novel stress tolerant (abiotic and biotic), highly productive and resource efficient forages to drive livestock production and productivity for market oriented small and medium, size farm operations in Eastern Asia and Eastern Africa
column17: Good quality feed year-round is limiting livestock productivity on-farm and resource use in farms of small to medium size. Feed production can amount to 50 to 70% of livestock production costs. Forages are a means to overcome the feed gap, and resilient forages responding to different abiotic and biotic stresses, including low soil fertility, drought / excess water, pest diseases, are essential, increasing livestock productivity by up to 15%. To scale such technologies, suitable entry points i.e., market-oriented livestock production particularly dairy are required. Enablers are animal genetics and health technologies which capitalize on the improved feeding as well as capacity and dissemination channels such as cooperatives and functional seed supply systems. We are using a diversity of advanced forages which have a good availability of seed and/or planting material and demand pull through livestock production in Kenya; at the same time a pipeline for improved forages is being maintained.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for improved chickens, animal services and markets for women farmers, delivered by women veterinarians in tanzania in Tanzania, United Republic
column17: A package combining gender accommodative and transformative approaches to deliver improved chickens, animal services and markets to women farmers by women veterinarians. Gender accommodative approaches were adopted to enhance the business and chicken management skills of the women vets. Gender transformative approaches (in this case social media) were adopted to address gender norms that make women’s involvement in chicken business socially inappropriate. Restrictive gender norms are considered the root cause of gender-based disadvantage; unlike gender accommodative approaches, gender transformative approaches aim to change such restrictive norms for lasting social change.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for the women's empowerment in livestock index(weli) for measuring women's empowerment in systems where livestock is important for livelihood in Tanzania, United Republic
column17: The WELI facilitates assessments of the impact of livestock interventions on the empowerment of women involved in the sector. By getting better at understanding what interventions work best at providing empowering opportunities, we can refine these interventions and in the long term, provide better empowering opportunities for women involved in livestock. Providing women farmers with opportunities for empowerment through livestock is important to both enhance household livelihoods and nutrition while also promoting progress on gender equity. In 2015, the International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI), in collaboration with Emory University developed the WELI tool based on the Women’s Empowerment in Agriculture Index (WEAI) developed earlier by IFPRI. The WELI measures women’s empowerment in livestock and crop agriculture and focuses specifically on key areas of livestock production, such as animal health, breeding and feeding; and on use of livestock products, such as animal-source-food processing and marketing.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for testing point of cow, a penside diagnostic test, for treatment decision making in mastitis in Kenya
column17: Point of Cow is a disposable chip manufactured by Fluimedix (Denmark).  It is a compact and user-friendly diagnostic tool that serves as a crucial component in antibiotic treatment decision making. The chip is engineered to detect both Gram-negative and Gram-positive bacteria within 4-24hrs,  enabling quick decision-making on whether to use antibiotic treatment for mastitis. Point of Cow is primarily designed for dairy farmers, but can also be used by milk processors and quality control professionals in the dairy industry. It is a valuable tool for anyone involved in milk production and processing.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for an innovative genetic improvement strategy for sheep and goat that involves the end users, farmers, in the design and implementation of the scheme in Ethiopia
column17: Breeding programs that are community-based cover a range of situations. Typically, they target low input systems with farmers within a limited geographical area who have a common interest to work together for the improvement of the genetic resources of their animals. Community-based breeding programs (CBBPs) focus on indigenous stock and consider farmers’ needs, views, decisions and active participation, from inception through to implementation. Most importantly, they provide a participatory and bottom-up approach. CBBP combines farmer training to improve selection methods, consisting of pooling community flocks to create a larger gene pool from which breeding animals can be selected, scientific support to provide farmers with information on different breeding options and data collection to monitor how well individual animals perform. The entire community flock is treated as one. Livestock keepers who choose to participate in the program are organized into sheep/goat breeding associations, many of which later evolve into formal cooperatives.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for cassava peel as a nutritious animal feed for livestock feed suppliers and livestock-keepers in Nigeria
column17: In Nigeria, processing cassava for food and industry yields around 15 million tons of wet peels annually. These peels are usually dumped near processing centres to rot or dry enough to be burned. Rotting heaps release methane into the air and a stinking effluent that pollutes nearby streams and underground water, while burning produces clouds of acrid smoke. However, when properly dried, peels can be an ingredient in animal feed. Previous attempts over two decades to use peels in animal feed failed to yield profitable options for drying wet peels at commercial scale, but recent research suggests that cassava peels can be processed into high-quality cassava peel (HQCP) products to be used as nutritious, low-cost animal feed ingredients by livestock feed suppliers and their customers (livestock-keepers)

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for pigsmart digital extension platform for enhancing farmers knowledge in climate smart best practices in herd health, genetics, feeding and manure management in Uganda
column17: PigSMART platform delivers digital extension messages to pig farmers. It covers an integrated content that is delivered to pig farmers based on the stage of growth of the pigs. The messages include best practices in feeding, herd health management, breeding and genetics, manure management and heat stress management. The process of integrating and adapting the content followed key steps: (i) curation of research outputs on feeds, health, genetics, and heat stress, (ii) drawing messages from the research outputs, (iii) validating messages from the researchers and government extension  to ensure integrity of content, (iv) integrating messages premised on the different stages of pig growth, and (v) developing audio skits from integrated content in Luganda. A brochure on the integrated content was developed and disseminated to pig farmers in addition to the audio skits. The messages can be used by extension agents to train farmers on best practices in pig production.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for A digital decision support tool to help farmers to produce improved animal diet on farm by balancing nutrients, processing roughages and mixing feed ingredients in proper proportion in Southern Asia
column17: The tool is a mobile based application that can be used by extension agents and farmers to balance their animals’ diet by matching nutrients required by the animal (for body mainetance, production and reproduction) and their availability in the feed offered. The application selects the cheapest locally available feeds to bridge the nutritional gap.  The suggestions are given in the form of an advice memo, which includes guidelines for efficient use of different feeds. Additional information such as the nutrient gap, cost of purchased feeds and additional income before and after balancing the diet are also given.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for institutional and business models for scaling and commercialization of forages and forage seeds in mixed farming systems in ethiopian highlands in Ethiopia
column17: The Africa RISING Ethiopian Highlands project, a predecessor to the Mixed Farming System Initiative validated and promoted various forage species. The limiting factor for wider diffusion and adoption has been limited supply of forages and forage seeds. In this activity, we want to test various integrated commercialization models. The commercialization model want to test include an integration of land clustering, contractual agreement with forage seed companies, formal field inspection and cost-benefit analysis.  Commercialization of forage seed production in Ethiopian highlands is a mixed farming system challenge as sustainable intensification of forage seed production requires collaboration of multiple forage seed sub-system stakeholders and management of trade-offs and synergies with crop production as forages and crops production compete within the limited available land of smallholder farmers.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for dynamic evolutionary populations of productivity of mixtures of different of barley in ethiopian highlands in Ethiopia
column17: Maintaining inter-varietal crop diversity, created through evolutionary plant breeding (EPB), on farms is proven to improve farmers productivity, resilience to climate change and enhance dietary diversity. We have tested evolutionary populations created through Evolutionary Plant Breeding in Ethiopia, Bhutan, Iran, Jordan, Nepal and Uganda for four crops: Barley, beans, wheat and rice and identified superior performing populations under different farming systems. Integration of evolutionary plant breeding to Sustainable Intensification of Mixed farming System (SI-MFS) in target countries is important to sustain crop production sector of target farming systems. At least one composite or mixture population is developed for each country targeted by the SI-MFS initiative.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for  assessment on improving water use efficiency to increase agriculture productivity in mid-hills of nepal through micro irrigation practices by international water management institute in Nepal
column17: Insufficient water availability in the mid-hills of Nepal, including many municipalities in Khotang and Surkhet districts, has negatively impacted agricultural productivity in the region. During the participatory innovation selection process for various components of the Mixed Farming System, local farmers identified micro-irrigation as a top-priority innovation to enhance agricultural output. In July 2023, 179 participants (107 women and 72 men) were trained in micro-irrigation techniques and efficient water use practices. As a result, 70 drip irrigation kits and 113 sprinkler kits were distributed, with a focus on supporting disadvantaged farmers. Ongoing support has been provided for the installation and operation of these climate-smart and gender-friendly kits, in coordination with the respective municipality and ward offices. Some of the farmers from the piloting area have reported that the kits have helped increase vegetable production in their homestead gardens.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for co-development and delivery of agro-climatic bulletin (acb) through public systems to provide climate advisory to inform local agricultural planning, decision making, and adoption of climate adaptive farm practices in vietnam   in The Socialist Republic of Viet Nam
column17: The Agro-Climatic Bulletin (ACB) is an approach that provides climate advisory services to smallholder farmers in Vietnam using seasonal, monthly, and 10-day weather forecasts. It is co-developed and implemented through national and sub-national public institutions, with integration into agricultural planning and decision-making. At the national level, the Plant Production and Protection Department secured approval from the Ministry of Agriculture and Environment for an allocated budget of VND 3,916,800,000 (USD 150,000) to scale ACB nationwide between 2026 and 2028, bringing total government investment to about USD 201,000 for 2023–2028. Provincial partners are also mobilizing additional local funding to strengthen implementation. ACB is recognized as a technical advancement and supports national initiatives such as the National Action Plan to Adapt to Climate Change (2021–2030), the 1 Million Hectares and the Digital Transformation Programs. PPPD has issued official directives to sustain ACB implementation and reorganize Technical Working Groups following administrative restructuring in 2025.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for mbili mbili and doubled-up legume are innovative cropping system innovations to ensure crop diversification and crop resilience in farming systems, especially favorable to smallholder farmers with small land holdings. in Malawi
column17: Mbili Mbili intercropping system has been promoted as a crop diversification and intensification approach. Mbili-Mbili (two maize rows alternating with two legume species) exploits plant spatial configurations to increase light penetration to the legumes, otherwise often shaded by cereals. The aim is to increase legume productivity while maintaining the same productivity of the cereal and taking advantage and complementarity of the different growth habits and durations of the combined crops. It enables farmers to grow both legumes and cereals on the same land and thus harvest at different times. In the event of a loss, one crop serves as insurance. This makes the system climate-smart. Mbili Mbili system has been reported to have a higher return (up to 37% more) compared to the standard farmer intercropping practices. The technology has been promoted in maize-growing areas in east and southern Africa, and was formally released in Malawi as agronomic innovation.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for basal npk fertilizer timing, cowpea living mulch and leaf stripping for intensification of smallholder maize-livestock farming system in northern ghana in Ghana
column17: The innovation is a bundle of three technologies for intensification of maize-small ruminants farming system in northern Ghana. The basal NPK fertilizer timing focuses on applying the fertilizer at planting stage of maize to reduce nutrient stress especially during the emergence-vegetative stage, enhance nutrient use efficiency and yield. Intercropping of cowpea at one week after planting of maize as a living mulch provides soil surface cover, increases soil moisture retention, adds nutrients through biological nitrogen fixation, suppresses weeds growth, and increases yield and food diversity. Harvesting of maize leaves below the cob leaf at silking stage (Leaf stripping) offers quality forage for livestock without compromising grain yield. The stripped maize leaf forage has a 40% higher crude protein content than the crude protein content of feed required for the body maintenance of livestock. Feeding strip maize leaf to small ruminants increases live body, slaughter, and carcass weights.

column17: The call for establishing the Tropical Poultry Platform (TROP) has emanated from the need to address the critical bottlenecks constraining the efficient and effective operation of poultry value chains in the tropics. SAPLING will identify key actors and catalyse TROP’s creation. Working alongside national, regional, and private sector partners, we will engage and collaborate with partners, exploiting synergies and complementarities and ensuring alignment and harmonization of actions with like-minded institutions. Key private sector players in the poultry industry, investors, farmers’ groups/associations, civil society organizations and non-governmental organizations. Considering the above, TROP focuses on existing innovation platforms as well as other initiatives. The partnerships to be forged could be crystallized through project implementation/investment proposal agreements, Collaborative Research Agreements, memoranda of understanding and/or simple transactional/contractual arrangements. TROP will be established as a membership-based organization that would mobilize resources both from within its members as well as from potential outside financiers.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for layanan konsultasi padi (rice crop manager indonesia): a digital advisory service for rice farmers in indonesia in Indonesia
column17: Rice Crop Manager Indonesia, known locally as Layanan Konsultasi Padi (LKP), was developed and introduced to address the key challenges for rice production and productivity in Indonesia through site-specific recommendations leading to a proven increase in yields and incomes. LKP is a digital agriculture decision support tool developed by the International Rice Research Institute to identify the best nutrient management practices for specific rice fields using site-specific nutrient management principles. LKP is designed for use by extension workers, crop advisors, input providers, and providers of services who interview a farmer using a computer or smartphone. Collected information is used to calculate recommendations and transformed into a crop management guideline for the farmer in a one-page printout. Each guideline provides an actionable recommendation, which matches the location-specific cropping practices and needs of a farmer.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for high-frequency diet quality data collection and mapping  in Rwanda and Guatemala
column17: The innovation is end-to-end integrated system that combines citizen engagement for data curation with modern agile analytics to provide real-time and actionable insights about dietary patterns and food system dynamics. The system is made up of three components: citizen-powered high-frequency data collection, user-centered dashboard analytics, and demand-driven reflexive modeling of intervention options. The innovation stands out by leveraging crowdsourced data collection methods that are both cost-efficient and easily deployable, enabling more frequent and accurate insights compared to traditional in-person methods on diets, markets, and transport infrastructure. It aims to serve as scalable platform to engage, inform, and empower individuals and decision-makers; support data-driven and informed decision-making; and provide robust data to inform policies and interventions, direct capital investments to improve food system resilience, and increase preparedness/planning for potential and direct risk. It is already under development with diet quality, food flows, and transport network being mapped in Rwanda and Kenya.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for Development of a Digital Twin for water resources management in the Limpopo River Basin in southern Africa in Southern Africa
column17: Water resource management in any basin, like the Limpopo River Basin with its intermittent supplies, is complex due to factors like rainfall, water allocation, quality, ecosystems, and risk to citizens. Balancing these factors often exceeds most managers' capabilities, despite the existence of numerous data sets. ; This project aims to develop a Digital Twin, a real-time, data-backed digital replica of the ground situation. Enhanced with machine learning and AI, it will integrate available data and models, providing easy and intuitive access to information. Grounded in real data, its outputs will be of tangible value, making it indispensable to water resource managers once fully developed.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for mdii: a multidimensional index designed to promote ethical and socially inclusive digital innovation processes within food, land, and water systems.
column17: Digital innovations are increasingly being utilized in food, land, and water systems. It's crucial that these innovations are inclusive and cause no harm, especially for less developed countries where many people rely on food systems for their livelihoods. However, there is a lack of standard metrics and guidelines for measuring and promoting digital inclusivity. To address this gap, the Multidimensional Digital Inclusivity Index (MDII) has been developed. The MDII offers 22 indicators of digital inclusivity across five dimensions. It can be used to assess and promote the level of digital inclusivity of an innovation, an innovation bundle, an organization, or a country. This index aims to make digital innovations accessible, usable, beneficial, participatory, and safe for socially and economically marginalized groups in food systems.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for longa: an artificial intelligence-based audio analytics tool for identifying farmers' need and targeting digital extension services in Tanzania, United Republic, Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria
column17: The increasing capabilities of Artificial Intelligence (AI)-augmented data analytics present significant opportunities for agricultural extension organizations operating in the Global South. In this work, we developed a proof-of-concept audio analytics tool to demonstrate the possibility of automating the process of translating and analyzing farmers' voice message data collected by Farm Radio Rural radio programs. This innovation, Tambaya ("Ask" in Hausa) draws on several cutting-edge AI tools, in particular, the use of unsupervised learning to generate language models, to expand the number of languages available to the user. In the context of NGOs working with African (Tanzania, Uganda, Kenya and Nigeria) radio stations, Tambaya will allow them to quickly analyze farmers' voice messages, understand farmers' needs, and draw insights to deliver targeted extension services.

The CS-MAP indicates climate-related risks classes and location-specific adaptation plans for crop production at district level and act as decision support tool. The CS-MAPs are vital tools especially to implement in the world’s most critical food basket; delta, in changing climate and hence having scaling needs. The scaling readiness assessment has been carried out for climate smart risk map tool and its implementation enablers though a 1-day workshop.

column17: Conservation Agriculture (CA) is based on three key principles: minimum soil disturbance, provision of permanent soil cover and the use of rotations or associations amongst other good agriculture practices. These CA principles are applicable to a wide range of crop production systems from low-yielding, rain-fed conditions to high-yielding, irrigated conditions. However, the techniques used may vary from place to place depending on farm power, system management conditions and farmer circumstances. CA aims at rebuilding the soil, optimizing crop production inputs especially labour, and increasing profits. The social and economic benefits gained from combining production and protecting the environment under CA, including reduced input and labour costs, are greater than those from production alone. With CA, farming communities become providers of more healthy living environments for the wider community through reduced use of fossil fuels and through conservation of environmental integrity and services.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for a web-based based decision support tool for managing rift valley fever outbreaks in kenya  in Kenya
column17: Rift Valley fever (RVF) is a zoonotic disease caused by a virus that is transmitted by a wide range of mosquitoes. The disease mainly affects livestock and people. It has been listed by the World Health Organization as one of the nine diseases that has the potential to cause pandemics. Decision makers often face major challenges predicting and responding to outbreaks, and so we have developed this prototype tool for forecasting risk and identifying actions that can be taken to manage the risk. The tool has two components, the first ingests rainfall forecasts from the Global Precipitation Climatology Centre and processes anomalies to identify periods when above normal rainfall is expected. The second component provides actions that need to be taken at various phases of the outbreak ranging from pre-outreak, outbreak, post-outbreak and peacetime periods.

column16: Innovation Package and Scaling Readiness assessment for risk-contingent credit product, aimed at increasing farmers access to production credit and protecting financial institutions against the risks of credit default in Kenya, Zambia and Ethiopia
column17: Risk-contingent credit (RCC) is a linked financial product that embeds within its structure an insurance protection which, when triggered, offsets loan payments due to the lender. RCC mitigates drought-related agricultural risks and provides access to credit for smallholder farmers, requiring minimal collateral. Building on existing partnerships and field collaboration, the current project intends to (1) improve the RCC product to minimize basis risk in product design by incorporating key environmental variables from state-of-the-art remote sensors, along with measurements from weather stations; (2) integrate a gender dimension into RCC analysis by including intra-household and cluster-level randomized controlled trials (RCTs) to reach, benefit, and empower women farmers; (3) develop formal relations with an increasing number of RCC service providers for piloting RCC in Kenya, Zambia, and Ethiopia; and (4) build capacity on risk management through finance and agronomy trainings for farmers in Kenya and Ethiopia, and development of outreach and guidance materials.

column16: Innovation Packaging and Scaling Readiness Assessment Progress Report of Aflasafe for Sub-Saharan Africa: Accelerating National Scaling in Malawi to Strengthen Food Safety and Inclusive Staple Crop Value Chains
column17: The project focuses on developing and scaling Aflasafe technology to combat aflatoxin contamination in key agricultural crops across Sub-Saharan Africa. It aims to reduce aflatoxin levels in maize, groundnuts, and sorghum, ensuring food safety and compliance with international standards. By applying biocontrol strategies, the initiative addresses mycotoxin contamination to enhance food quality, protect public health, improve market access, and promote sustainable agricultural practices in affected regions.; ; As aflatoxin contamination continues to threaten public health, food safety, and trade, Innovation Packaging and Scaling Readiness (IPSR) workshops were convened in Mozambique and Malawi to accelerate nationwide scaling of Aflasafe. Using IPSR tools, participants conducted readiness assessments, feasibility scoring, and mini-strategy development to identify barriers and produce draft acceleration plans to guide coordinated scaling efforts.
